SYNTHETIC TEST DOCUMENT - FICTIONAL PATIENT - NOT FOR CLINICAL USE
COLONOSCOPY REPORT
Facility: Riverside Teaching Hospital Endoscopy Unit (fictional)
Patient: Agnes Thorley (fictional)
Date of service: November 2, 2026
Attending endoscopist: Rafael Duquesne, MD (fictional)
Fellow: Mina Halvorsen, MD (fictional), gastroenterology fellow
Indication: Chronic watery diarrhea; personal history of colon polyps.
History: In March 2024 Dr. Corwin Platt (fictional) performed a colonoscopy elsewhere.
At that procedure Dr. Platt (fictional) removed a 4 mm rectal polyp with hot biopsy forceps.
Procedure: The fellow advanced the colonoscope to the cecum under my direct supervision.
The fellow removed a 7 mm descending colon polyp with a cold snare under my direct supervision.
I took random cold forceps biopsies of the right and left colon for microscopic colitis.
I was present for the entire procedure, from insertion to withdrawal of the colonoscope.
Findings:
- Descending colon: 7 mm sessile polyp, removed with a cold snare as above and retrieved.
- Colonic mucosa normal throughout; random biopsies taken from the right and left colon.
- Rectum: normal, with no residual polyp at the site treated in March 2024.
Impression:
1. 7 mm descending colon polyp, removed by cold snare.
2. Normal-appearing colonic mucosa; random biopsies taken to evaluate for microscopic colitis.
Plan: Await pathology.
